newsitem.title: USA: MGE white wheat ends up sharply on India talk.
newsitem.headline: MGE white wheat ends up sharply on India talk.

text.p: MGE white wheat futures settled higher and at new contract highs amid talk that U.S. white wheat may also be destined for India, traders said.
The nearby May contract rose four cents per bushel to settle at a new contract high of $4.36. New contract highs were also set in July, September and December, 1997.

It was reported earlier Wednesday that Australia sold one million tonnes of wheat to India for shipment beginning in August, but some traders at the Minneapolis Grain Exchange speculated that Cargill Inc may be involved in providing U.S. white wheat to India.

"We heard Cargill was buying all the white wheat they could buy today. They also sold a bunch of September $4.10 white wheat puts. So there's some thinking out there that maybe Cargill is selling white wheat (to India) out of the U.S.," a MGE trader said.
MGE white wheat futures settled four to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with July up 9-1/2 cents at $4.25. September was up 9-1/4 cents at $4.28-1/4.
The Grain Exchange estimated volume in white wheat futures totaled 444,000 bushels, up from 245,000 bushels Tuesday.
